goal: repurposable approved drugs for Alzheimer's disease
note: SYNTHETIC ILLUSTRATIVE BUNDLE — representative fragments and accessions demonstrating the run-bundle schema and the scorer, not a live literature-mined result. See README.

hypotheses.statement: The JAK1/2 inhibitor baricitinib may slow Alzheimer disease progression by dampening JAK-STAT-driven microglial neuroinflammation.

bridge_chain.claim: neuroinflammation is associated with Alzheimer disease
JAK-STAT pathway genes are upregulated in Alzheimer disease microglia

queries: consensus: does baricitinib treat Alzheimer disease?
opentargets: known drugs for EFO_0000249 containing baricitinib

disconfirming_searched: clinicaltrials.gov: baricitinib AND Alzheimer (no terminated-for-futility trials found)
opposing GEO signature: JAK-STAT downregulated in AD microglia (none found)
counter-mechanism: JAK inhibition impairing protective microglial function (weak, not decisive)
falsification_record.notes: CNS exposure of baricitinib is limited; flagged as a translational risk, not a falsifier of the mechanism.

hypotheses.experimental_test: In iPSC-derived human microglia challenged with oligomeric Abeta, baricitinib is predicted to reduce STAT1 phosphorylation and pro-inflammatory cytokine release (IL-6, TNF) dose-dependently and restore phagocytosis. Falsified if baricitinib produces no change in STAT1-P or cytokine output versus vehicle.

hypotheses.statement: The CysLT1 antagonist montelukast may reduce Alzheimer disease neuroinflammation via 5-lipoxygenase / leukotriene pathway suppression.

bridge_chain.claim: cysteinyl leukotriene signaling promotes neuroinflammation and BBB dysfunction
ALOX5 (5-LOX) is upregulated in Alzheimer disease hippocampus
ALOX5 is associated with Alzheimer disease

queries: pubmed: montelukast AND (Alzheimer OR dementia) [tiab] before 2020
consensus: does montelukast treat Alzheimer disease?
opentargets: known drugs for EFO_0000249 containing montelukast

disconfirming_searched: clinicaltrials.gov: montelukast AND Alzheimer (no failed cognitive-endpoint trial before cutoff)
opposing GEO signature: ALOX5 downregulated in AD (none found)
counter-mechanism: peripheral-only action with no central engagement (montelukast has measurable CNS penetration)
falsification_record.notes: Central exposure is modest but nonzero; the leukotriene axis is independently supported by the GEO ALOX5 signal.

hypotheses.experimental_test: In aged 5xFAD mice, chronic montelukast is predicted to lower hippocampal cysteinyl-leukotriene levels and microglial activation markers and improve Morris water-maze performance versus vehicle. Falsified if neuroinflammatory markers and behavior are unchanged despite confirmed central drug exposure.
